def-smooth-principal-g-bundle:
## Definition

Let $G$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie group, $M$ a smooth manifold, and $P$
a smooth manifold. A **smooth right principal $G$-bundle** is a right principal
$G$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ in the topological sense of
[[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]], with the following
additional smooth structure: $\pi$ and the right $G$-action are smooth, and
the principal-bundle charts can be chosen as equivariant diffeomorphisms
$\pi^{-1}(U)\cong U\times G$. Thus each chart respects the projection to
$U$ and the right action on the $G$ factor. The smoothness convention is that
of [[def-smooth-map-between-manifolds-with-boundary]]; boundaryless manifolds
are the default in this item.

The topological principal-bundle clause retains its free, transitive right
action on every fibre and its local triviality. Smoothness adds compatible
differentiable structure; it does not select a connection or assert that a
global trivialization exists. The empty-base case is allowed and then $P$ is
empty by the cited topological definition.
def-principal-connection-and-vertical-cu:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as recorded by
[[def-countable-choice]], and let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal
$G$-bundle in the sense of
[[def-smooth-principal-g-bundle]]. The tangent bundle $TP$ has the canonical
smooth structure supplied by
[[thm-the-tangent-bundle-has-a-canonical-smooth-2n-manifold-structure]]. Its
**vertical subbundle** is
$$VP:=\ker(d\pi)\subseteq TP.$$
In each principal chart $U\times G$, this is the tangent bundle in the $G$
factor, so it is a smooth vector subbundle of $TP$ in the sense of
[[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]].

A **principal connection** on $P$ is a smooth vector subbundle $H\subseteq TP$
such that $T_pP=V_pP\oplus H_p$ for every $p\in P$ and
$$d(R_g)_p(H_p)=H_{pg}\qquad(p\in P,\ g\in G),$$
where $R_g(p)=pg$ is the principal right action. Thus $H$ is a smoothly varying
horizontal complement to the vertical tangent directions, invariant under the
structure-group action. This definition is conditional on a specified $H$;
it is not an existence theorem for connections on every bundle.

Let $h:TP\to H$ and $v:TP\to VP$ be the projections given by this direct-sum
decomposition. For smooth vector fields $X,Y$ on $P$, define the
**vertical-valued curvature** by
$$K_H(X,Y):=-v([hX,hY]),$$
where the vector-field bracket is the commutator
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. This formula is tensorial in
$X,Y$: for a smooth function $f$,
$$v([f hX,hY])=f\,v([hX,hY])-hY(f)\,v(hX)=f\,v([hX,hY]),$$
because $v(hX)=0$, and the same calculation in the second input gives
$v([hX,f hY])=f\,v([hX,hY])$. It is alternating because the bracket is
alternating. Consequently the formula defines a smooth alternating bundle map
$TP\times_P TP\to VP$, rather than depending on which local vector-field
extensions represent the tangent vectors.

This item uses the vertical-valued convention. It does not identify $VP$ with a
Lie-algebra-valued form or assert a Maurer–Cartan formula. Its axiom base
contains $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ exactly through the canonical tangent-bundle
and vector-field suppliers above; the displayed splitting and curvature
formula themselves select no objects from a family.
def-gauge-group-of-a-smooth-principal-bu:
## Definition

Let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle as in
[[def-smooth-principal-g-bundle]]. A **smooth gauge transformation** of $P$ is
a smooth diffeomorphism $\Phi:P\to P$ satisfying
$$\pi\circ\Phi=\pi,\qquad \Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g\quad(p\in P,\ g\in G).$$
Here diffeomorphism has the meaning of
[[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]. The **gauge
group** $\mathcal G(P)$ is the set of these transformations under composition.
The identity satisfies the two conditions, compositions preserve them, and
the inverse of such a $\Phi$ also covers $M$ and commutes with the right
$G$-action: writing $q=\Phi(p)$ gives
$\Phi^{-1}(qg)=\Phi^{-1}(\Phi(p)g)=\Phi^{-1}(\Phi(pg))=pg$. Hence these maps
form a group under the composition law of [[def-group]].

The structure group $G$ acts on each fibre of $P$, while $\mathcal G(P)$ acts
on the total bundle by automorphisms over the identity map of $M$. They are
different groups: a gauge transformation may vary from fibre to fibre, and
this definition assigns no topology or finite-dimensional Lie-group structure
to $\mathcal G(P)$.
prop-gauge-transformations-act-on-princi:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $P\to M$ be a smooth right principal
$G$-bundle with a principal connection $H$, and let
$\Phi\in\mathcal G(P)$. Then
$$\Phi_*H:=d\Phi(H)$$
is a principal connection. If $K_H$ and $K_{\Phi_*H}$ are the vertical-valued
curvatures from
[[def-principal-connection-and-vertical-curvature]], then for
$X,Y\in T_pP$,
$$K_{\Phi_*H}(d\Phi_pX,d\Phi_pY)=d\Phi_p(K_H(X,Y)).$$
Composition makes this a left action of $\mathcal G(P)$ on the set of
principal connections.
prop-gauge-transformations-induce-associ:
## Statement

Let $G$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie group, let $P\to M$ be a smooth right
principal $G$-bundle, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space, and
let $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ be a smooth representation, where
$\operatorname{GL}(V)$ is the group of invertible linear maps $V\to V$. Write
$\mathcal G(P)$ for the gauge group of
[[def-gauge-group-of-a-smooth-principal-bundle]]. Put
$E_\rho:=P\times_\rho V$ for the associated smooth vector bundle of
[[def-associated-bundle-to-a-principal-bundle-and-representation]] and
[[thm-associated-vector-bundle-is-well-defined]]. For every
$\Phi\in\mathcal G(P)$ define
$$\overline\Phi:E_\rho\to E_\rho,\qquad [p,v]\longmapsto[\Phi(p),v].$$
Here a smooth vector-bundle automorphism means a smooth fibrewise-linear
diffeomorphism covering $\operatorname{id}_M$. The map $\overline\Phi$ is such
an automorphism, and
$$\overline{\Phi\circ\Psi}=\overline\Phi\circ\overline\Psi,\qquad \overline{\operatorname{id}_P}=\operatorname{id}_{E_\rho}.$$
Thus $\Phi\mapsto\overline\Phi$ is a group homomorphism to the group of smooth
vector-bundle automorphisms of $E_\rho$. If $\Gamma^\infty(E_\rho)$ denotes
the smooth sections as in
[[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]], then
$$\Phi\cdot s:=\overline\Phi\circ s$$
is a linear left action of $\mathcal G(P)$ on $\Gamma^\infty(E_\rho)$. No
injectivity or surjectivity of either induced action is asserted.

The square below records the quotient descent, where $q:P\times V\to E_\rho$
is the orbit projection. It commutes because $\Phi$ is $G$-equivariant; the
pointwise verification appears in step 1.1.

```tikzcd
P \times V \arrow[r, "\Phi \times \mathrm{id}_V"] \arrow[d, "q"'] & P \times V \arrow[d, "q"] \\
E_\rho \arrow[r, "\overline{\Phi}"'] & E_\rho
```
